english: Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers and let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=[x](x-a)+[2x](x-b)$, where $[t]$ denotes the greatest integer less than or equal to $t$. If $f$ is continuous at every point of the interval $\left(\dfrac{5}{4},\dfrac{9}{4}\right)$, then the value of $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to3^{-}}f(x)$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $a$ तथा $b$ वास्तविक संख्याएँ हैं तथा $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=[x](x-a)+[2x](x-b)$ द्वारा परिभाषित है, जहाँ $[t]$, $t$ से कम या उसके बराबर महत्तम पूर्णांक को दर्शाता है। यदि $f$ अन्तराल $\left(\dfrac{5}{4},\dfrac{9}{4}\right)$ के प्रत्येक बिन्दु पर सतत है, तो $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to3^{-}}f(x)$ का मान ______ है।
solution: In $\left(\dfrac54,\dfrac94\right)$, $[x]$ jumps only at $2$ and $[2x]$ only at $\dfrac32$ and $2$; elsewhere $f$ is a polynomial
At $x=\dfrac32$: $[x]=1$ on both sides, $[2x]$: $2\to3$; jump $=\dfrac32-b=0\Rightarrow b=\dfrac32$
solution_full: $f$ is continuous wherever both $[x]$ and $[2x]$ are locally constant. In $\left(\dfrac{5}{4},\dfrac{9}{4}\right)$, $[x]$ changes only at $x=2$, and $[2x]$ changes only where $2x$ is an integer, i.e. at $x=\dfrac{3}{2}$ and $x=2$.

At $x=\dfrac{3}{2}$: $[x]=1$ near $\dfrac32$; $[2x]=2$ for $x<\dfrac32$ and $3$ for $x\ge\dfrac32$. So $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to3/2^{-}}f=\dfrac12-a+2\left(\dfrac32-b\right)$ and $f\left(\dfrac32\right)=\dfrac12-a+3\left(\dfrac32-b\right)$. Continuity gives $\dfrac{3}{2}-b=0$, so $b=\dfrac{3}{2}$.

At $x=2$: for $x<2$, $[x]=1$ and $[2x]=3$; for $x\ge2$, $[x]=2$ and $[2x]=4$. So $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to2^{-}}f=(2-a)+3(2-b)$ and $f(2)=2(2-a)+4(2-b)$. Continuity gives $(2-a)+(2-b)=0$, so $a=4-b=\dfrac{5}{2}$.
With these values $f$ is continuous on the whole interval (the end points $\dfrac54$, $\dfrac94$ are not jump points, and $x=1$, $x=\dfrac52$ lie outside).
Left-hand limit at $3$: for $\dfrac52\le x<3$, $[x]=2$ and $[2x]=5$, so $f(x)=2\left(x-\dfrac52\right)+5\left(x-\dfrac32\right)\to2\cdot\dfrac12+5\cdot\dfrac32=1+\dfrac{15}{2}=\dfrac{17}{2}$.
originality_note: New: two greatest-integer factors with different step sizes multiply linear factors; continuity on a chosen interval forces exactly the two jump conditions inside it (at 3/2 and at 2), which fixes a and b, and then a one-sided limit at another jump point is asked (way 5). Closest known: f(x) = [x] sin(pi x) or [x](x - a) continuous at integers. Different because: the student must locate which jump points of [x] and [2x] lie in the interval and treat the double jump at x = 2.

concept_use.Evaluation of limit involving GIF and fr: One-sided limits of [x] and [2x] at 3/2, 2 and 3 give the jump conditions and lim_{x->3-} f = 17/2.
concept_use.Continuity and Differentiability of func: Continuity of f on (5/4, 9/4) requires zero jumps at 3/2 and at 2, giving b = 3/2 and a = 5/2.
